lead.kicker: TOP STORY  •  SAUDI ARABIA AND YEMEN
lead.headline: Houthis Declare Saudi Airports “Legitimate Targets”
lead.deck: Saudi officials count at least 20 deaths at airports between October 6 and 11.
body: The Houthis, an Iran-aligned movement holding Sanaa and parts of north-west Yemen since 2014, are fighting Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces. A UN-brokered truce in place since 2022 has collapsed. After a strike on Sanaa airport, the Houthi leader set out a tit-for-tat policy: “airports for airports, ports for ports, and a blockade for a blockade.”

The Saudi-backed Yemeni government says the Sanaa strike was meant to stop an Iranian plane landing there. The Houthis have declared the kingdom’s airports and airspace “legitimate targets,” except Mecca and Medina, and say they have also hit Aramco facilities, including a gas plant and a refinery.

Saudi civil aviation authorities report at least 20 deaths and 356 injuries at airports between October 6 and 11. The deadliest strike, on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport on October 10, killed at least 12, including an American citizen. Dammam, Abha, Jazan and Najran airports were also hit. On Wednesday the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted a missile fired toward Riyadh. Houthi claims could not be independently verified.

lead.why: The Bab el-Mandeb strait, at the Red Sea’s southern end, is a key route between the Mediterranean and Asia, and its importance has grown because the Iran conflict has effectively closed Hormuz. Control of it is disputed.

world.headline: Russia Targets All Three of Kyiv’s Heat and Power Plants
world.deck: Zelenskyy says at least 600,000 people are without power as winter nears.
body: In the overnight barrage of October 13-14, Ukraine’s prime minister, Serhii Koretskyi, said all three of Kyiv’s combined heat and power plants came under attack. Combined heat and power plants produce electricity and heat for homes from one fuel supply. Officials said everyone at the plants was evacuated and nobody was hurt there; repairs are under way.

Koretskyi said critical facilities in Kyiv Oblast that supply the capital and central Ukraine were also struck. President Zelenskyy said significant damage had been caused to 26 energy sites and that at least 600,000 people were without power, adding that more blackouts were possible.

The strikes followed US President Donald Trump’s announcement of an “energy ceasefire.” Zelenskyy said he would honour a deal if Moscow did, but had seen no Russian approval. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov would not say whether Russia had agreed, saying only “Contacts are ongoing.”

india.headline: Delhi Police Remove Jantar Mantar From Protest Venues
india.deck: A standing order names Ramlila, Burari and CBD grounds; courts are now involved.
body: A Delhi Police standing order dated October 11, issued by Commissioner Anurag Kumar, de-notifies Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site. It names Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground and CBD Ground, East Delhi as replacements. Some outlets described a circular issued on October 12, probably the same decision released later. A detailed SOP for the new venues will follow.

The order says it follows recommendations of a Union Home Ministry committee. Indian Youth Congress president Uday Bhanu Chib has challenged it in the Delhi High Court. Police told the court the decision was based on a Supreme Court order of October 9, and a separate plea against the standing order is pending before the Supreme Court.

The move came as protests against the Election Commission and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar drew heavy police action. Cockroach Janta Party leaders were detained near Jantar Mantar after trying to enter the site.

politics_and_civics.headline: Three Weeks to US Midterms: Congress Is on the Ballot
politics_and_civics.deck: All 435 House seats and 35 of 100 Senate seats are up on November 3.
body: Midterm elections take place in the middle of a US president’s term. On November 3, 2026, voters will choose all 435 members of the House of Representatives and 35 of the 100 senators. The result decides which party controls each chamber of Congress.
Coverage frames the vote as a referendum on President Trump, and the balance of power in Congress will shape his room to act. Cost of living is a central concern for voters.
Alongside Congress, governors and state legislatures are also being elected in many states.
politics_and_civics.why: Congress passes laws and controls federal spending, so control of either chamber changes what a president can achieve.

economics.headline: US Inflation Rose to 3.7% in September
economics.deck: Costlier gasoline pushed prices up 0.6% in a month, the most in five months.
body: Inflation measures how fast prices rise. The US Labor Department reported on October 14 that consumer prices in September were 3.7% higher than a year earlier, up from 3.4% in August. Gasoline was the main driver.
Prices rose 0.6% from August to September, the biggest monthly gain in five months. Prices excluding food and energy, which show underlying pressure, rose 2.6% over the year, up from 2.4%.
Higher inflation puts pressure on the Federal Reserve, which meets October 27-28 and raised its target range to 3.75%-4.00% in September, its first hike since 2023.

science_and_technology.headline: Webb Data Reveal the Lopsided Edge of an Exoplanet’s Atmosphere
science_and_technology.deck: A Cornell-led team mapped WASP-17b in a Nature Astronomy paper on October 14.
body: An exoplanet is a planet orbiting a star other than the Sun. WASP-17b is a scorching gas giant about 1,300 light-years away, per Cornell and Bristol. Astronomers often treat the outline of such a planet’s atmosphere as a circle when they study starlight passing through it.

The team used a technique called transmission strings, which measures the distance from the planet’s centre to the atmospheric edge at many points, using James Webb Space Telescope data. The edge was slightly lopsided: it reaches farther on the evening side, while the cooler morning side is less extended. Winds carry heat from the day side to the night side, which drives this asymmetry.
Water and carbon dioxide were found fairly consistently around the edge, even as temperature and shape varied. The differences were broadly consistent with theory and earlier models, Cornell said.

illustration.subtitle: WASP-17b

science_and_technology.why: Peer-reviewed methods like this let astronomers test models of weather on worlds too far to ever visit.

explainer.title: How is the US Congress elected?
body: Congress has two chambers. The House of Representatives has 435 members, who serve two-year terms, so every seat is up at each election. The Senate has 100 members, two per state, who serve six-year terms, so only some seats are up at a time.

That is why this year’s midterms put all 435 House seats and 35 Senate seats on the ballot. Midterms fall halfway through a president’s four-year term, which makes them a common test of the president’s popularity.
